deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from p.12 and this page: M is a small category of 'models' sitting in its presheaf category M̂. Each model n has an underlying finite poset J_n with a largest element d_n and a strictly increasing 'length' τ_n: J_n → N. The analogy is the face poset of a simplex or of a cell. B_0 ⊂ M̂ is the full subcategory of 'admissible' objects X. Such an X is the union (sup) of its subobjects isomorphic to models. In addition, for model subobjects K, L ⊂ X, the intersection K ∩ L is the sup of the model subobjects it contains. To such an X Grothendieck attaches the poset K = X̃ of its model subobjects. He equips it with an 'M-épinglage' (M-pinning), defined on p.12:
(a) a strictly increasing map τ_K: K → N;
(b) for each ξ ∈ K with n = τ_K(ξ), an isomorphism u^K_ξ: J_n ≅ K_{≤ξ} sending d_n to ξ. The maps u^K_ξ are called 'admissible'.
This page adds two axioms.
(1) Compatibility with length: τ_K ∘ u^K_ξ = τ_n.
(2) Transitivity: for ξ ∈ K and η ∈ J_n, put n' = τ_n(η) and ζ = u^K_ξ(η). Then u^K_ξ ∘ u^n_η = u^K_ζ, where u^n_η: J_{n'} ≅ (J_n)_{≤η} is the pinning of the model poset J_n itself.
In modern terms, (K, τ, u) is a poset each of whose principal down-sets is coherently identified with a model face poset. This is a generalized CW poset or cellular poset, structured so that its cells are modelled on M.
Claim 1: the groupoid of admissible objects of M̂ (isomorphisms only) is equivalent to the groupoid of M-pinned ordered sets.
Claim 2: arbitrary maps between such objects can also be reconstructed. They are the strictly increasing maps f: K → L that satisfy (a) τ_L ∘ f = τ_K and (b) compatibility with pinnings: for η = f(ξ), the restriction f|K_{≤ξ}: K_{≤ξ} → L_{≤η} satisfies f ∘ u^K_ξ = u^L_η, as maps from J_n with n = τ_K(ξ) = τ_L(η).
On p.14 he deduces that f is a local isomorphism on down-sets. He then specializes to injective f, which correspond to monos. Closed (down-)subsets inherit a unique induced pinning.
Purpose: a combinatorial, poset-theoretic description of 'regular' or 'non-singular' presheaves over a category of cell-models. Examples are non-singular semi-simplicial sets, ordered simplicial complexes, and regular cell complexes. This presumably prepares the ground for treating such objects (stacks/fibrations over them) through their face posets.
errors: In the triangle the target is written K_{≤η}; it must be L_{≤η}. p.14 indeed writes L_{≤η}. This is a slip.

The claim that arbitrary morphisms in M̂ between admissible objects are exactly τ-preserving, pinning-compatible strictly increasing maps needs a hypothesis left implicit. It requires that all maps of M are monomorphisms (M direct/semi-simplicial-like, no degeneracies), or that morphisms are restricted to non-degenerate ones. Otherwise a presheaf map can collapse a model onto a smaller one, and its effect on face posets is not strictly increasing or length-preserving.
Strict monotonicity of f is redundant once τ_L∘f = τ_K and f is order-preserving with local isos. This is harmless.

The equivalence of groupoids also implicitly requires that the pinned poset can be realized as an admissible presheaf. That is, the colimit of models over the pinned poset must recover a presheaf whose model subobjects are exactly K, and the intersection condition must hold. This is asserted, not proved, on this page.

ideas.what: Poset of non-degenerate cells, with each principal down-set identified coherently with a model face poset (M-épinglage), axioms (1)-(2)
ideas.modern_name: CW poset / cellular poset; face poset of a regular CW complex or of a non-singular (semi-)simplicial set; 'regular' presheaves on a direct/Reedy category
ideas.usually_credited_to: Björner (CW posets, 1984); for simplicial: classical (ordered simplicial complexes); more recently regular/non-singular simplicial sets (Waldhausen–Jahren–Rognes; Fjellbo; Campion–Kapulkin–Maehara)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses posets and cellular models of homotopy types, but this specific pinning formalism is not known to me in his published texts

ideas.what: Equivalence between the groupoid of admissible (regular) presheaves on M and the groupoid of M-pinned posets, with morphisms reconstructed as pinning-compatible maps
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction of regular/non-singular presheaves from their face posets (nerve–face-poset correspondence)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Björner for regular CW complexes

ideas.what: Down-closed subsets inherit a unique induced pinning making the inclusion admissible; injective maps correspond to monos

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates an axiomatic, model-category-independent notion of an 'M-pinned poset'. It works for an arbitrary category of cell-models M, not just simplices. He identifies these with regular presheaves on M. This is a general framework close to later work on regular Reedy categories and regular presheaves, but it is only sketched and is routine in substance.
missed.quote: La catégorie dont les objets sont les objets admissibles de M̂, les flèches les isomorphismes entre eux, est équivalente à celle des ens. ordonnés M-épinglés
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly historical interest. It shows an early Grothendieck use of face-poset combinatorics for general cell shapes in the context of stacks. It anticipates the 'regular presheaf' viewpoint, but there is no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but essentially folklore correspondence between regular presheaves on a category of cell models and coherently 'pinned' posets, analogous to Björner's CW posets. The generality over an arbitrary model category M is mildly interesting historically, but a specialist would not be surprised.
transcription_corrections: 'ens adoucis M-iso-glés' should read 'ensembles ordonnés M-épinglés' (cf. 'M-épinglage' on p.12 and 'M-épi-gl.' on p.14).
'les homs quelconques {+dans Ĉ ...}' is probably 'les flèches quelconques dans M̂ entre tels objets'. 'Ĉ' is likely a misreading of M̂.
'en reconstituant également' should read 'se reconstituent également'.
In the diagram, the target is written 'K_{≤η}' in the manuscript; L_{≤η} is meant.
The crossed-out line reads '[-si ξ∈K, η∈K, alors-]'. The word above it ('enfin') is uncertain.
The handwriting before ∀ in (2) is a struck-out symbol; the equation is u^K_ξ ∘ u^n_η = u^K_ζ with ζ = u^K_ξ(η).
